quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' strategy regarding contract extensions and the second apron
quotes.excerpt: Jim Dolan is on the record saying, we're not going into the second apron.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Jim Dolan is on the record saying, we're not going into the second apron, and then the Knicks operated their off-season not going into the second apron. It cost them Mitch Robinson and they drove a hard bargain with Landry Shamet. I thought they got him at a good number. So they have set the standard that they're not doing it. So Karl-Anthony Towns, he's a 20 and 10 guy who's proven to be a champion and was great in the playoffs. He wants that max extension. It is completely reasonable.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: They got all their guys at good numbers. They did.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's contract sacrifice and the impact on Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson is going to come get all of his money.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: Jalen Brunson is going to come get all of his money. Every bit that he signed the year early, right? He could have signed for $100 million more by signing later. Every dollar of that 280 or 300 that he's supposed to get next summer, he's going to get all of that. How does that affect any of this conversation? That affects what you do with Karl-Anthony Towns. Karl-Anthony Towns wanted an extension before the season started, did not get it. Now we're in this spot where Karl-Anthony Towns sacrificed a lot, wound up going into the playoffs as their most important player. You saw how critical he was to them rolling through the East, them rolling through the finals, his defense on Victor Wembanyama. Usually when that happens, a player wants to get rewarded for his sacrifice. How do the Knicks balance both of those things? Is it possible to do both of those things? Because you know Jalen Brunson is going to have to eat first, but Karl-Anthony Towns is going to be up first for a contract extension.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' long-term roster construction and the second apron pressure
quotes.excerpt: It's hard to keep teams together for more than like three years at this point.
quotes.quote: It's hard to keep teams together for more than like three years at this point. And for that to happen, you have to bend somewhere. The Thunder, the Celtics, you saw what's happened to the Celtics. The Thunder are bending trying not to break, and the Knicks are, it's tight. It feels, it's squeezed. And so we'll see, do they bend or break? And that's what this moment will be an indication of whether that could happen.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Denver Nuggets' roster stability and the Paint Watson situation
quotes.excerpt: They're the same team and they still have the Paint Watson situation to figure out here.
quotes.quote: The Jokic one is fascinating. For me it's interesting, and I know he's come out and said that Denver is where he's going to be and all that and he's going to sign next year, but man, I'm just looking at their roster, what they've done or really haven't done this off-season, and going into next year, they're the same team and they still have the Paint Watson situation to figure out here.
